structured_output.what_is_happening: YesBlob (YES) is a Pump.fun token about 12.7 days old that graduated to PumpSwap. It has come back to life at about a $2.34M market cap, near its all-time high: the ATH price is 0.00278 and the current price is 0.00238. In the last hour, volume was $160k against $152k of liquidity, and one-hour volume was 3.4x the six-hour average rate. Most of the six-hour and 24-hour activity happened in that single hour: 895 of 1,070 six-hour buys and 808 of 926 six-hour unique buyers. Sellers outnumber buyers in every window (1,031 vs 808 unique over one hour). Price is up 16% over the hour but down 10–11% over the last five minutes. The move comes alongside 30 active paid DexScreener boosts, a community-takeover (CTO) profile and a recycled project X account.

narrative.description: 'YesBlob' looks like a blob-style mascot meme, maybe tied to a 'yes' reaction image. The X handle 'yesblobhood' fits the '-hood' community-meme naming style. No project description exists. The GeckoTerminal twitter field points to a specific tweet (h0lygyatt/status/...), which suggests the token is based on a single viral post or image. Its image is duplicated 3 times, so it isn't a unique asset.
narrative.why_spreading: The packet shows no organic spread. The burst lines up with a CTO profile update and 30 paid boosts, which points to push-driven attention rather than a story catching on outside the token's own promoters. One-hour unique buyers (808) are real breadth, but sellers are the larger group, which looks like existing holders using the liquidity to exit.

token_connection.why_this_token: The name 'YesBlob' is fairly specific, and this is the only YES token with meaningful current volume. The ticker YES itself is generic and heavily reused.
token_connection.competing_tokens: Eight other YES tokens exist. One ('YES', 4tJp…rise) has about $543k of liquidity and mcap but no volume. The others are dead joke coins ('Will This Coin Go Up?', 'Vote Yes', etc.). None competes on the YesBlob name.

authenticity.evidence: There are 30 active paid DexScreener boosts, a CTO flag and a recently updated profile. The project X account has been renamed three times (dresweev43705 → rainbow_catsol → yesblobhood), with the latest rename about 6 days ago, so it was recycled from another token's CTO. The dev closed out their position. Wallets include 14 bundlers, 18 snipers and a 31% bot/degen rate. There are no smart-money signals, no degen calls and no renowned or KOL wallets. On the positive side, holders are widely spread: top 10 hold 6.4% (GMGN says 3.65%), across 4,200 holders.
authenticity.uncertainty: There is no X data, so a genuine viral post behind the meme can't be ruled out. The 19 smart wallets have unknown timing.

structural_risks: Unique sellers outnumber buyers in every window, a sign of distribution into the spike
Price is dropping 10–11% in the last five minutes after the one-hour pump
Liquidity is about 6.5% of market cap; a CTO token with boost-driven flow can unwind quickly
RugCheck flags unlocked or low LP, which conflicts with GMGN's LP burn ratio of 1.0 (PumpSwap LP is usually burned)
Price is close to the ATH, which likely acts as resistance where earlier holders sell
The X account is recycled and has pivoted between tokens before

structured_output.counterargument: Holders are unusually well spread for a $2M token: 4,200 holders with the top 10 under 7% and no dev or insider concentration. Nearly 800 unique buyers in an hour is real participation, not a handful of wallets. A funded CTO team running 30 boosts may keep pushing. A ~13-day-old token revisiting its ATH with broad breadth could break out, and mascot-blob memes have caught on before. The heavy selling could simply be healthy two-way turnover.
unknowns: Whether a real viral 'yes blob' post or image is behind this (no X data)
When the 19 smart wallets bought and whether they are selling
Who funds the CTO boosts and how long the push can last
What set off the one-hour burst (a call channel, a KOL, or the boosts alone)

source_coverage.notes: No internet in this condition; this judgment uses only the evidence packet.

structured_output.thesis: This is a burst driven by a CTO and paid boosts on a recycled X account, with no evidence of a story spreading on its own. Sellers outnumber buyers during the spike, and price is already slipping from near the ATH. Holder spread is healthy, so a crash is not the base case. The more likely outcome is that attention fades over the next six hours.
